inline_comments.comment: The default value of `false` directly contradicts the PR description, which says "The button is shown by default for all inline stories — no configuration needed." With `?? false`, users must explicitly opt in by setting `parameters.docs.canvas.resetButton = true`; the button will never appear without extra configuration. If the intended behavior matches the PR description, the default should be `true`. If the feature is intentionally opt-in, the PR description needs to be corrected and this parameter should be documented.

When `resetButton` is `false` (the current default), `handleResetStory` is defined but never used. The `useCallback` dependency array is still evaluated. Consider moving the `useCallback` inside a conditional or gating it on `resetButton && inline` to avoid creating an unnecessary callback on every render for the common case where the button is disabled.

`UndoIcon` semantically implies "undo the last action" to most users, not "reset everything to defaults." Since this button resets all story args (or triggers a full remount, depending on which event ends up being used), an icon like `RefreshIcon` or `SyncIcon` would better communicate the intended "reset to initial state" semantics and avoid confusion with the browser/OS undo gesture.

The ActionBar visibility condition is growing: `withSource || onResetStory || additionalActionItems.length > 0`. As more optional actions are added this pattern will keep expanding. Consider extracting a derived boolean like `const hasActions = withSource || onResetStory || additionalActionItems.length > 0;` above the return and referencing it here for readability.

general_comments.comment: No automated tests are added for this new feature, and all test checkboxes in the PR checklist are unchecked. At minimum there should be: (1) a unit test for `Preview` that verifies the "Reset story" button renders when `onResetStory` is provided and does not render when it is absent, and (2) a unit/integration test for `Canvas` that verifies the correct event (`FORCE_REMOUNT` or `RESET_STORY_ARGS`, whichever is intended) is emitted on click. Without tests, it is easy for the conditional gating logic (`inline && resetButton`) or the event name to silently regress.

The PR description and the code use inconsistent names for the button. The description says "Add a 'Reload story' button" and refers to it as a reload action, while the button text in the code says "Reset story" and the parameter is named `resetButton`. This ambiguity (reload vs. reset) reflects the underlying confusion between `FORCE_REMOUNT` (reload/remount) and `RESET_STORY_ARGS` (reset args), and will make it harder for future contributors to understand the intent of the feature.
